svg.title: NGINX
svg.desc: NGINX. A reverse proxy and web server: TLS termination, load balancing, caching and rate limiting in front of applications. Step 1, Where it sits: NGINX meets every request for shop.example: it ends TLS, serves /static/ and proxies /api/. Step 2, Event-driven workers: One worker per core, one event loop each: least_conn sends GET /api/products/42 to app-2. Step 3, Cache, limits, failures: A HIT never reaches the apps; a client past 10 r/s and a queue of 20 gets 429; app-2 is skipped. Step 4, Reload, and the limits: nginx -s reload: new workers start, old ones finish and exit. Limits: static config, Plus features.

g.text: NGINX meets every request for shop.example: it ends TLS, serves /static/ and proxies /api/.
One worker per core, one event loop each: least_conn sends GET /api/products/42 to app-2.
A HIT never reaches the apps; a client past 10 r/s and a queue of 20 gets 429; app-2 is skipped.
nginx -s reload: new workers start, old ones finish and exit. Limits: static config, Plus features.
Every request for shop.example reaches NGINX first. It ends TLS, serves /static/ from disk, and passes /api/ to the catalog
app servers behind a cache and a per-client rate limit. A Kubernetes ingress controller does the same job; often a cloud LB sits in front.
The master reads nginx.conf and starts one worker per CPU core (worker_processes auto). Each worker serves all its connections
from one event loop (epoll on Linux), not a thread per connection. least_conn picks app-2, the least busy, over a kept-alive connection.
A second GET /api/products/42 within 60 s is a HIT: no app server is called. 203.0.113.7 goes past 10 r/s and fills its queue of 20:
the next request gets 429 (limit_req_status; the default is 503). app-2 fails a 3rd time within 10 s, so it is skipped for 10 s; app-3 answers.
nginx -s reload: the master checks the new nginx.conf and starts new workers with it; the old ones stop accepting, finish their requests and exit.
new upstream servers need a reload (or DNS resolve)
active health checks: NGINX Plus only
per-request policy: an API gateway or Envoy
